FORM has direct HBM test evidence through probe-card products, SK hynix recognition, and Q1 2026 DRAM/HBM demand commentary; it is a strong Layer 1B test-node candidate.

KLIC is a plausible but less proven advanced-packaging equipment candidate; thesis requires proof that TCB, APTURA, vertical wire, memory, and heterogeneous integration products are becoming material HBM/AI revenue drivers.

The node is best mapped into four investable public-market subnodes: OSAT capacity, HBM/advanced-package inspection and metrology, HBM wafer/stack probe cards, and advanced bonding/interconnect equipment.

Need a later layer to add non-US primary listings or ADR/OTC-accessible Taiwan/Korea/Japan names such as Powertech-like OSATs, substrate suppliers, test-handler vendors, and consumables suppliers; this pass was constrained to US-listed companies.
AMKR should remain the US-listed OSAT reference anchor for HBM/advanced-packaging overflow, but it is not the cleanest underfollowed name because its AI packaging angle is increasingly visible.
FORM is a strong HBM-adjacent test candidate because probe cards and known-good-die testing become more valuable as HBM stacks and heterogeneous packages become more expensive.
COHU is a lower-attention backend-test and handler candidate; survival to later layers requires evidence that AI/HPC package handling, contactors, and inspection are material to orders or margins.

KLIC is an underfollowed advanced-packaging equipment candidate where the key verification point is whether thermocompression and chip-to-wafer advanced-packaging tools are becoming material versus legacy bonding cyclicality.

The node appears more investable in US listings through test/probe/handler/bonding equipment and Amkor-like OSAT capacity than through pure memory-overflow OSATs, many of which are Taiwan/Korea/Japan listed.

Need a later pass on non-US-listed Powertech, ASE, Advantest, Disco, Tokyo Electron packaging tools, Ibiden/Shinko substrates, and Japanese/Korean materials to benchmark whether US-listed candidates are secondary proxies or true chokepoints.
AMKR should remain in the node universe as the most direct US-listed OSAT/advanced-packaging overflow candidate, but its thesis must be separated from generic OSAT cyclicality.
FORM should remain in the node universe as an HBM testing-gate candidate because company materials explicitly connect its probe cards to HBM testing and SK hynix.
COHU should remain in the node universe as a low-attention HBM backend test-handler candidate, with direct but currently modest disclosed HBM revenue.

KLIC is a relevant follow-up candidate for a later Layer 1B or Layer 2 pass because thermocompression bonding and advanced packaging tools have explicit HBM/AI packaging links, but the current four-candidate cap prioritized TSM reference plus AMKR/FORM/COHU.

The key falsification test for this node is whether candidate revenue is driven by AI/HBM/advanced packaging intensity rather than only broad memory-cycle beta or semiconductor capital-equipment recovery.

AMKR should be retained as the US-listed OSAT reference anchor for the HBM/advanced-packaging overflow node; its thesis must be tested against AI/HPC advanced-packaging revenue mix rather than generic OSAT cycle exposure.
FORM is a strong underfollowed HBM-adjacent test candidate because company filings explicitly connect DRAM probe-card growth to HBM designs used in generative AI.

COHU is a small/mid-cap discovery candidate with explicit HBM inspection/metrology orders, but the current disclosed HBM revenue base appears small; survival in later layers depends on 2026 scaling evidence.

KLIC belongs in the speculative-underfollowed advanced-packaging equipment watch list; the evidence supports AI/CPO/heterogeneous-integration exposure, but HBM-specific materiality needs verification.

This pass did not include non-US-listed but highly relevant Asian names such as Powertech, ASE, Advantest, Disco, Tokyo Electron, and substrate/material suppliers; a separate non-US pass is needed for the full chokepoint map.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around HBM and advanced-packaging overflow capacity. The cleanest direct exposures found in this pass are not the obvious HBM producers or AI accelerator customers, but US-listed OSAT, advanced-packaging equipment, probe-card/test, and inspection/metrology companies. Amkor is the reference OSAT anchor; Camtek and FormFactor have direct HBM-related order/product evidence; Kulicke & Soffa is a more indirect advanced-packaging equipment name tied to thermocompression bonding, heterogeneous integration, CPO, and memory/high-compute packaging. These are research candidates only, not recommendations. Layer 1B expansion found a compact US-listed universe around HBM-adjacent test, advanced packaging equipment, OSAT capacity, and backend memory-test overflow. The reference lane is represented by Amkor as the most direct US-listed OSAT anchor. The underfollowed lane is stronger in tools and test-adjacent suppliers than in pure OSATs: FormFactor for HBM wafer/probe-card test, Cohu for AI/advanced-package handlers and inspection/test automation, and Kulicke & Soffa for thermocompression / chip-to-wafer advanced-packaging equipment. Powertech-like overflow exposure remains important context, but Powertech itself is not US-listed, so it is not included as a candidate. Expanded the node from obvious AI accelerator and foundry leaders into US-listed second-order beneficiaries around outsourced advanced packaging, HBM-adjacent wafer/probe testing, backend test handlers, and bonding/advanced-packaging tools.
